solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Walked in shallow water, or rowed in boat

definitions.meaning: to wade about at the seaside, feet in the shallows
to propel a canoe or small boat with a single-bladed oar

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one verb form: a seaside splash in the shallows and moving a canoe along with an oar.

clue.text: Someone attractive and fashionable embraced by young boxer?

indicators.note: embraced by puts the fashionable word inside the young dog's word

parts.note: a boxer is a dog breed, so a young one is a pup
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A handsome trendy type cuddled by a teenage fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter; the question mark warns it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A poster model or glamorous figure whose picture is stuck on a wall is someone attractive.

clue.text: Country people initially put off motorway drive

indicators.note: initially says the deterring and motorway pieces come at the start, before the people

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
the M1 is Britain's first main motorway, its 1 read as letter I
a nation is the people of a country

explanation.surface: Rural folk are first to be deterred from motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its digit stands for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of ambition, grit and resolve is a synonym of steely resolve.

clue.text: Some scholar googles "Music by Handel"

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An academic searches online for a Handel piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's famous aria Ombra mai fu, from Serse, is popularly known by this tempo title.

clue.text: S African port, for a start definitely not rural

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: urban means of the town, the opposite of rural

explanation.surface: A South African harbour city, certainly not countrified to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A major harbour city on South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal coast.

clue.text: Puzzle concerning naval vessel turning over

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a business letter

indicators.note: turning over says the vessel's word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a naval vessel

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a warship capsizing.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle in which images and letters stand for words is a classic word-game type.

clue.text: Impatient, note, to reach Cornwall resort shortly

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: shortly means the resort's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip

explanation.surface: Restless to get to a Cornish seaside town soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but signals docking the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless, fidgety person who resists control is impatient.

clue.text: Sons tried pub's exotic Chinese food

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: The boys sampled the pub's unusual oriental dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese delicacy made from the edible saliva nests of swiftlets.

clue.text: Desire to have animals raised in part of East London

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Wanting to rear livestock in an East London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like rearing animals; it turns YENPETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A district in the borough of Tower Hamlets, in London's East End.

clue.text: Character with book showing area of countryside

parts.note: someone's nature is their character or temperament
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A personality trait combined with a volume reveals a stretch of rural land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a noun beside 'Character' but works as the verb meaning to make a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected tract of land kept for wildlife is a kind of countryside area.

clue.text: A person selling pieces of wood, maybe: backing for garden structure

indicators.note: backing means the whole phrase is run in reverse, from its end to its start

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood, given by example
a rep, short for sales representative, is a person who sells

explanation.surface: A timber salesman's support for something built in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a rep who sells logs, so the logs come before the seller; 'backing for' turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: An arched framework over a path, carrying climbing plants, is a garden structure.

clue.text: One book by Sterne? Oddly, a different writer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: oddly says take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the novelist's surname

explanation.surface: Is one book by Laurence Sterne secretly the work of another author?
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy; the answer is the Norwegian playwright, hence 'a different writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House is an author other than Sterne.

clue.text: Mischief makers behind church — they're little monkeys

indicators.note: behind places the troublemakers after the church abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: imps are mischievous little sprites or children

explanation.surface: Naughty children larking about at the back of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little monkeys' is the affectionate term for naughty kids, with a nod to the apes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful young apes, or cheeky children, are loosely called little monkeys.

clue.text: Maybe Derby girl is enlisted by commander-in-chief

indicators.note: enlisted by puts the girl inside the commander's abbreviation, as if signed up into the ranks

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman from Derby joins up under the top general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the city; it is the Epsom horse race, one of England's five great flat races.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby at Epsom is one of the five English flat-racing Classics, an example of the type.

clue.text: Nip round, meeting merry king for a drink

indicators.note: round means the small word is turned about and read backwards
merry, as in tipsy, suggests the monarch's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pop out to meet a jolly monarch for a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip' looks like a verb meaning to pop out; read backwards it gives PIN, then KGIN rearranges king.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and Angostura bitters, a classic naval tipple.

clue.text: Just me, playing lyre

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Only me, strumming a lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is kept as it is; 'playing' rearranges only lyre, giving RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms in the sense of nothing more than.

clue.text: Changes American aims

parts.note: ends are goals or aims, as in means to an end

explanation.surface: The United States revises its goals.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or revise a text, as a law is altered, is to change it.

clue.text: Saga inevitably reduced in length once more

indicators.note: cutting the phrase short at both ends leaves a run of letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A long story that always ends up being abridged.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten 'Saga in(evitably)' by its first letter and most of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing a thing once more is doing it a second time.

clue.text: On day after Feb 28, talk endlessly about union

parts.note: in a non-leap year the day after 28 February is 1 March, written MAR I

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Discussing a marriage on the first of March, at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about union' is adjectival: concerning marriage, the union of two people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things concerning a marriage, the union of a couple.

clue.text: During break one's to take another test

indicators.note: during places the single letter inside the word for a break, as something happening within it

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
one is I; the 's, read as is, links it to the rest of the clue

explanation.surface: A student uses the holiday to sit an exam again.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an examination a second time after failing it.

clue.text: Compare Alfie regularly with little Kenneth

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the name, here the second and fourth

parts.note: Ken is the short form of Kenneth

explanation.surface: Setting Alfie side by side with young Kenneth.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a likeness or comparison between two things is to compare them.

clue.text: How one might go and dispose of some fishing tackle?

definitions.text: How one might go and dispose of some fishing tackle?

parts.words: How one might go and dispose of some fishing tackle?
parts.note: a British slang phrase for clearing off, read literally as throwing away an angler's barbed lure

explanation.surface: Packing in angling by throwing out the gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang for leaving or clearing off, taken literally as tossing away a fish-catching barb.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for leaving or clearing off, literally throwing away part of an angler's kit.

clue.text: Clergyman shot in billiard hall, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: in billiards a cannon is a shot where the cue ball strikes two other balls in turn

explanation.surface: A priest gunned down in a snooker hall, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a shooting; it is the billiards stroke in which the cue ball hits both other balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter holds this title.

clue.text: Attack puts one out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Assault knocks someone unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to assail someone violently, as when thugs jump a passer-by.
